title: Schema-driven event sinks for streaming LLM output
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a schema-driven EventSink abstraction for the Python SDK that converts streaming LLM output (token chunks / delta events) into validated, typed objects (pydantic/dataclasses) and emits them at logical boundaries. Goal is to make structured streaming easy and robust for app code: incremental parsing, boundary-safe validation, idempotent delivery semantics, and backpressure-aware emission.
acceptance_criteria: EventSink interface defined with clear lifecycle (open, accept_chunk, flush_boundary, close)
Adapters implemented for Pydantic BaseModel and Python dataclasses with minimal runtime allocations
Two parsing modes supported: framed NDJSON/JSONL and incremental JSON patch assembly
Backpressure buffer and max-buffer-bytes configuration, default 1MB, prevents unbounded memory growth
Integration test demonstrating streaming chat -> EventSink -> list[Model] with correct ordering and exactly-once semantics under retries
Documentation + code example in SDK docs showing both strict and lenient validation modes
tasks: Write design doc and API surface (internal RFC)
Implement EventSink abstract base class and concrete PydanticAdapter
Add incremental JSON frame parser (supports NDJSON and simple delimiter-based framing)
Integrate with existing streaming iterator used by Python SDK (stream.parse_stream())
Add configuration knobs: buffer_size_bytes, validation_mode (strict|lenient), emit_on_partial_boundary
Write unit tests and integration tests including simulated network retries and token reordering
Add examples to docs and a short cookbook snippet for chat -> structured events
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial design sketch. Motivating use-cases: structured chat messages, tool call streams, and analytics events emitted during generation.
2026-03-03 - Diego Ramos: Reviewed RFC; suggested explicit framing contract rather than guessing by content length. Prefer NDJSON by default for compatibility with existing tooling.

2026-03-05 - Maya Chen: Implementation note - avoid per-token pydantic validation (expensive). Validate once at logical boundary; provide a low-cost incremental schema check to catch obvious corruption earlier.
2026-03-07 - Liam O'Connor: Pushed initial EventSink ABC in PR 1458. Integration tests added for simple NDJSON event stream.
2026-03-09 - QA (Priya Singh): Found an edge case where partial JSON docs cross chunk boundaries; added test to assert correct reassembly and no double-emission on retry.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Decided to expose two validation modes: strict (raises on first schema error) and lenient (emit object with .validation_errors metadata).
decisions: Framing: default to NDJSON/JSONL for event streams; provide plug-in parser for other framing when needed
Validation: perform full model validation at boundary emission to avoid per-token overhead. Provide optional incremental checks for early failure detection
Idempotency: EventSink will assign monotonic sequence ids for emitted events and persist a short-term in-memory seen-set while the stream is open to avoid double-emits during transient retry behavior
Backpressure: provide buffer_size_bytes with configurable eviction policy (by default: block upstream read when buffer exceeded) to protect SDK client memory
Error handling: lenient mode emits objects with validation_errors metadata and continues; strict mode aborts/raises and surfaces to caller
tests: unit: PydanticAdapter validates correct fields and attaches validation_errors in lenient mode
integration: end-to-end streaming chat producing 5 structured events over network with simulated chunk splits
perf: throughput benchmark comparing validate-at-boundary vs validate-per-token (target < 20% overhead)
e2e: sample app cookbook that consumes streaming events into a database (sqlite) and asserts ordering / idempotency
